- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/02 (Sun) 10:19
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] One popular song from the 13th century is "Sumer is icumen in" (also known as the "Summer Canon" or the "Cuckoo Song").
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] "Sumer is icumen in" is a Middle English round or rota and is one of the oldest known musical compositions featuring six-part polyphony.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The lyrics of "Sumer is icumen in" celebrate the arrival of summer and the joys of nature.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The original Middle English text of "Sumer is icumen in" is provided:
  - Sumer is icumen in,
  - Lhude sing cuccu!
  - Groweþ sed and bloweþ med
  - And springþ þe wde nu,
  - Sing cuccu!
  - Awe bleteþ after lomb,
  - Lhouth after calue cu.
  - Bulluc sterteþ, bucke uerteþ,
  - Murie sing cuccu!
  - Cuccu, cuccu, wel singes þu cuccu;
  - Ne swik þu nauer nu.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] A modern English translation of "Sumer is icumen in" is provided:
  - Summer has come in,
  - Loudly sing, cuckoo!
  - The seed grows and the meadow blooms,
  - And the wood springs anew,
  - Sing, cuckoo!
  - The ewe bleats after the lamb,
  - The cow lows after the calf.
  - The bullock stirs, the stag farts,
  - Merrily sing, cuckoo!
  - Cuckoo, cuckoo, well you sing, cuckoo;
  - Don't ever you stop now.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The language used in this song might be challenging for modern English speakers to understand and sing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If the user wishes to join in singing, they may want to practice the Middle English pronunciation and become familiar with the melody.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Alternatively, the user can enjoy listening to locals sing and appreciate the cultural experience.
